# Elicit — resolve one consequential uncertainty

Start with the user's context and inspect factual gaps yourself. Ask one focused
question only when the answer changes the outcome. Show a concrete consequence of
the plausible readings. Accept explicit decisions, including a later revision, and
stop when the uncertainty is resolved.

Challenge a claim when evidence contradicts it. Treat hesitation in context rather
than diagnosing a knowledge gap from a phrase. Explain a missing fact inline when
that suffices; no survey, reading quota or mandatory interview follows automatically.

Keep the choice with the user. Separate observed symptoms, supported causes and
proposed fixes. Use seek-probe for an empirical unknown and seek-mockup when the user
needs to try alternatives. Clarification grants no implementation authority.

Return the decision, operative reason and remaining uncertainty. The answer can stay
in chat. Save only on request or as needed for an already-authorized handoff, using
`references/saving.md`; do not manufacture a thought or task.
